reply_text:
I found one candidate from 2026, and it is borderline. Everything this year traces back to a single occasion: a closed-door investor meeting Liang held on 20 May 2026, during DeepSeek's first outside fundraising round. A transcript leaked in July 2026. No one has confirmed it, and Liang and DeepSeek have not verified it. I saw no 2026 essay, post, public interview or hearing by him.

- **The candidate:** Momentum Works' English translation of the transcript has Liang saying that "within a year the high-quality-data problem will be handled fairly well domestically." That is about AI training data in China, so whether it counts as an AI prediction rather than an operations forecast is your call. The source is a translation of a leaked text, not an official transcript.
- **Seen in search results but never opened:** Liang reportedly said that in China, within "one or two years," AI should roughly match foreign models, or "maybe this year" replace them. That is the strongest dated claim of the year. I saw it in search snippets for Fred Gao's Substack and two other sites. But Fred Gao's page and the China Research Collective page I opened both seemed to be cut short, and neither contained the line. Two Chinese full-text pages that should carry it would not load (one redirected to an error page, the other was blocked). So I haven't quoted it. Opening one of those pages is the obvious next check.
- **Left out:** He said the domestic chip ecosystem would prove itself "within a year," but that's a chip forecast, so it's excluded. The "ten months" and revenue figures are business numbers. "Ten percent of GDP" and the hope to narrow the US gap to "six to twelve months" have no deadline, and the second is only in an NYU Shanghai article's paraphrase. "This year's step is Agent" describes the present. Asked when continual learning would be solved, he gave no date.
